title: Network-guided identification and in vitro/in vivo validation of Withaferin A as an inhibitor of nuclear factor kappa B for spinal cord injury repair.
authors: Xie, Chenghu; Zhang, Cunxin; Zhang, Ying; Chen, Liyi; He, Xiao; Xie, Xinzhou; Li, Kang; Wang, Xiaodong; Lv, Chaoliang
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文通过网络药理学和分子对接筛选Withaferin A作为NF-κB抑制剂用于脊髓损伤修复，虽涉及蛋白-DNA互作（NF-κB与DNA结合）和分子对接，但核心是药物抗炎湿实验验证，缺乏AI/物理模拟深度建模，与TF-DNA互作机制研究关联有限。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Spinal cord regeneration after injury remains a major clinical challenge due to the persistent inflammatory microenvironment associated with immune cell infiltration. Withaferin A (WA), a natural anti-inflammatory steroidal lactone with potential NF-kappaB-modulating activity, was identified by network-based screening as a candidate for spinal cord injury (SCI) and selected for further study. PURPOSE: This study aimed to identify and evaluate potential anti-inflammatory small-molecule therapeutics for SCI using a network-based drug screening strategy. STUDY DESIGN: Experimental study combining computational drug screening, in vitro macrophage assays and in vivo SCI mouse models. METHODS: Network pharmacology identified 296 candidate drugs targeting 113 SCI-related genes. Five top candidates, selected for chemical diversity and accessibility, were tested in LPS-stimulated in vitro models for effects on macrophage polarization and cytokine release. Molecular docking was used to predict drug-target interactions. The lead compound, WA, was then evaluated in SCI mice for inflammation, angiogenesis, neuroregeneration and motor recovery. RESULTS: WA showed the strongest anti-inflammatory activity, dose-dependently inhibiting LPS-induced M1 polarization and TNF-alpha/IL-6 secretion while promoting M2 polarization and IL-4/IL-10 secretion. Integrated computational and experimental analyses identified Cys160 in a hydrophobic pocket of NF-kappaB p65 as the covalent binding site of WA. In vivo, WA modulated macrophage polarization, reduced inflammatory mediator secretion, increased VEGF immunoreactivity and promoted neuroregeneration and motor recovery. CONCLUSION: WA exerts significant anti-inflammatory and neuroregenerative effects in SCI models. It also increases VEGF immunoreactivity, suggesting a potential pro-angiogenic effect after injury. These findings support WA as a promising therapeutic candidate for SCI.
abstract_zh: 背景：脊髓损伤后的再生因与免疫细胞浸润相关的持续性炎症微环境而仍是一项重大临床挑战。Withaferin A（WA）是一种具有潜在NF-kappaB调节活性的天然抗炎甾体内酯，通过基于网络的筛选被确定为脊髓损伤（SCI）的候选药物，并入选进一步研究。目的：本研究旨在利用基于网络的药物筛选策略，识别并评估用于SCI的潜在抗炎小分子治疗药物。研究设计：结合计算药物筛选、体外巨噬细胞实验和体内SCI小鼠模型的实验研究。方法：网络药理学确定了296种靶向113个SCI相关基因的候选药物。根据化学多样性和可及性选出的五个首选候选药物，在LPS刺激的体外模型中测试其对巨噬细胞极化和细胞因子释放的影响。分子对接用于预测药物-靶点相互作用。随后，在SCI小鼠中评估了先导化合物WA对炎症、血管生成、神经再生和运动恢复的影响。结果：WA表现出最强的抗炎活性，剂量依赖性地抑制LPS诱导的M1极化和TNF-alpha/IL-6分泌，同时促进M2极化和IL-4/IL-10分泌。综合计算和实验分析确定NF-kappaB p65疏水口袋中的Cys160为WA的共价结合位点。在体内，WA调节巨噬细胞极化，减少炎症介质分泌，增加VEGF免疫反应性，并促进神经再生和运动恢复。结论：WA在SCI模型中发挥显著的抗炎和神经再生作用。它还增加VEGF免疫反应性，提示损伤后具有潜在促血管生成效应。这些发现支持WA作为SCI的有前景治疗候选药物。
